body:
A Mac app now exists beside the iPhone app, from the same code: Astra in its own window, the same four widgets for the desktop, and dictation to the agent in a small panel opened from the menu bar or with Control-Option-Space. It is installed as /Applications/Astra.app on the Mac mini.

Checked on that Mac: the app starts, the host's page loads in its window, the agent link and the menu bar item open the dictation panel, and the system lists its widgets. The iPhone app was re-checked in a simulator after the shared code changed.

Not checked: the Mac app has not been paired, no widget has been placed on a desktop, dictation was not tried with a microphone, and the app is not distributed to other Macs.

Two things went wrong during testing and were put right. An early version of the Mac test typed into the host's pairing page and sent a pairing request to the live host; it was denied and no session came of it. A screenshot meant to show Astra's window showed part of another window on the desktop; it was deleted and the Mac test takes no screenshots now.

A crash report from earlier in the day explained an open question from the iPhone work: the app can abort in the system's audio code on a machine without a microphone. Dictation now checks for a microphone first.

Details: docs/ADR-077-MAC-APP.md and progress/2026-10-09-mac-app.md.

metadata.summary: Mac app built and installed on the Mac mini; not yet paired or distributed
